lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: angles of elevation and depression

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: A 3-4-5 triangle, θ opposite the side 3. Find sin θ.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Express sin 33° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 147°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 57°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 123°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 33°, because sine and cosine are always equal

items.prompt: From a point 4 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 3 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
choices: cos θ = 3/4
sin θ = 3/4
tan θ = 4/3
tan θ = 3/4

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 and hypotenuse 13. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 5. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 10 and one leg 6. Find the other leg.
Express sin 19° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 161°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 71°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 109°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 19°, because sine and cosine are always equal

items.prompt: From a point 160 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 36 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
A right triangle has legs 10 and 24 and hypotenuse 26. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 10. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
